description.en: The method that just remembers: how it predicts, every distance and voting rule on the exam, how to choose k, and why scaling and high dimensions break it.
description.zh: 什么都不学、只靠记忆的方法：怎么预测，考试里的每一种距离和投票规则，k 怎么选，以及为什么特征缩放和高维会把它搞坏。

name.zh: k 近邻算法与惰性学习

description.zh: 对单位不同的特征直接用欧氏距离

description.zh: 用训练误差选 k（k = 1 永远最好）

description.zh: 以为维度很高时最近邻仍然很近

title.en: What it is: predict by remembering
title.zh: 它是什么：靠记忆来预测

text.en: **k-nearest neighbours** (k-NN) is the one method that does no learning in the usual sense. Training means *store every example*. To predict a new instance, find the $k$ stored instances closest to it and let them answer.
text.zh: **k 近邻**（k-NN）是唯一一个不做“学习”的方法。训练就是**把所有样本存起来**。预测新样本时，找出离它最近的 $k$ 个存下的样本，让它们来回答。

items.en: Compute the distance from the test instance to every training instance.
items.zh: 算出测试样本到每一个训练样本的距离。

items.en: Keep the $k$ closest: the *neighbours*.
items.zh: 留下最近的 $k$ 个，它们是“近邻”。

items.en: Combine their labels: **classification** returns the most common class; **regression** returns the average value.
items.zh: 合并它们的标签：**分类**返回最常见的类别；**回归**返回平均值。

text.zh: 除此之外，一切都是要你自己做的选择，课件把它们叫做四个问题。每一个都是本课的一节，也都是考试的常见题：

rows.zh: 特征向量；名义、有序、数值
多数票、反距离、反线性距离

rows.en: small k: jagged; large k: smooth
rows.zh: 小 k：锯齿；大 k：平滑

title.en: Why it is a model at all
title.zh: 为什么它也算一个模型

body.en: The stored data plus a fixed distance and a fixed voting rule *is* the model. The regions of space where the answer changes are never written down; they exist implicitly in the data. This is **lazy** (instance-based) learning; we return to it at the end.
body.zh: 存下的数据，加上固定的距离和固定的投票规则，*就是*这个模型。答案发生变化的那些区域从不被写下来，只隐含在数据里。这叫**惰性**（lazy，基于实例）学习，最后一节再回来讲它。

title.en: Representing a point: the feature vector

text.en: Distance needs numbers, so every instance becomes a **feature vector**. The deck's golf data has four features and one label (instance a: sunny, hot, high, FALSE → no); row a is the vector (sunny, hot, high, FALSE). Three kinds of feature need three treatments:
text.zh: 距离需要数字，所以每个样本都变成一个**特征向量**。课件里的高尔夫数据有四个特征和一个标签（样本 a：晴、热、高、FALSE → no），a 行就是向量（sunny, hot, high, FALSE）。三种特征，三种处理：

rows.zh: 没有顺序的取值（颜色、形状）

text.en: The deck's fruit example turns nominal features into a 0/1 vector. Colours, shapes and tastes become six columns; an apple is red, round, sweet:
text.zh: 课件的水果例子把名义特征变成 0/1 向量。颜色、形状、口味展开成六列；苹果是红、圆、甜：

text.en: The feature vector has $6$ entries. The deck leaves the apple's and banana's size as `?` (missing) and reads it as a match when comparing them. Note what one-hot does: it makes every pair of different values equally far apart, which is exactly right for nominal data (red is not “closer” to yellow than to blue).
text.zh: 特征向量有 $6$ 个分量。课件把苹果和香蕉的“大小”留成 `?`（缺失），比较它们时当作匹配。注意独热做了什么：任意两个不同取值之间距离都一样，对名义数据这正合适（红色并不比蓝色更“靠近”黄色）。

title.en: Distances for 0/1 features: Hamming, matching, Jaccard

text.en: For two instances $a, b$ of $m$ nominal (0/1) features, three measures count agreement in different ways. Work them on apple vs banana from the previous page.
text.zh: 两个有 $m$ 个名义（0/1）特征的样本 $a, b$，有三种数“是否一致”的方式。在上一页的苹果和香蕉上算一遍。

text.en: Hamming distance
text.zh: Hamming 距离

text.en: Count the positions where they differ. Apple vs banana: red, yellow, round and curved differ; sweet agrees; the missing size is read as a match. So $d = 4$.
text.zh: 数两个向量不同的位置。苹果与香蕉：红、黄、圆、弯都不同；甜相同；缺失的大小当作一致。所以 $d = 4$。

text.en: Simple matching distance
text.zh: 简单匹配距离

text.en: Here $k$ is the number of matching features and $m$ the total number of features. Same idea as Hamming, but a fraction, so it lies in $[0,1]$: $k = 2$ matches out of $m = 6$ gives $d = 1 - 2/6 = 2/3$.
text.zh: 这里 $k$ 是匹配的特征数，$m$ 是特征总数。想法同 Hamming，但是个比例，落在 $[0,1]$：$6$ 个特征里 $2$ 个匹配，$d = 1 - 2/6 = 2/3$。

text.en: Jaccard distance
text.zh: Jaccard 距离

blocks.tex: d = 1 - J = 1 - \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A \cup B|} = 1 - \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A| + |B| - |A \cap B|}

text.en: Treat each instance as the **set** of features that are on: $A = \{\text{red, round, sweet}\}$, $B = \{\text{yellow, curved, sweet}\}$. They share one element and together have five, so $J = 1/5$ and $d = 4/5$.
text.zh: 把每个样本看成“开着的特征”的**集合**：$A = \{\text{red, round, sweet}\}$，$B = \{\text{yellow, curved, sweet}\}$。它们共有 1 个元素，合起来 5 个，所以 $J = 1/5$，$d = 4/5$。

title.en: Why Jaccard exists: shared zeros say nothing
title.zh: 为什么要有 Jaccard：共同的 0 说明不了什么

body.en: Matching counts 0-0 as agreement, Jaccard ignores it. Two shoppers who both did not buy among 10,000 products have almost everything in common, which is useless. For sparse 0/1 data (baskets, word presence) use Jaccard; when 0 and 1 are equally informative (male/female) use matching or Hamming.
body.zh: 匹配距离把 0-0 也算作一致，Jaccard 不算。两位顾客在一万种商品里都没买的那些，几乎占了全部，毫无信息。稀疏的 0/1 数据（购物篮、词是否出现）用 Jaccard；0 和 1 同样有信息量（男/女）时用匹配或 Hamming。

text.en: The Dice coefficient $2|A\cap B|/(|A|+|B|)$ also ignores shared zeros but weights the overlap twice; here $2\cdot 1/6 = 1/3$. It is a monotone function of Jaccard, so for ranking neighbours the two give the same order.
text.zh: Dice 系数 $2|A\cap B|/(|A|+|B|)$ 同样忽略共同的 0，但把重叠算两次；这里是 $2\cdot 1/6 = 1/3$。它是 Jaccard 的单调函数，用来给近邻排序，两者给出同样的顺序。

prompt.en: Instances $a = (1,0,0,0,0,1)$ and $b = (1,0,0,0,0,0)$. Which statement is true?

label.en: Simple matching distance is $1/6$; Jaccard distance is $1/2$.
label.zh: 简单匹配距离是 $1/6$；Jaccard 距离是 $1/2$。

label.en: Both are $1/6$.
label.zh: 两者都是 $1/6$。

feedback.en: Jaccard drops the four shared zeros: only the two 1-positions count, $A \cap B = 1$, $A \cup B = 2$, so $d = 1/2$.
feedback.zh: Jaccard 不算那四个共同的 0：只看两个 1 的位置，$A \cap B = 1$，$A \cup B = 2$，所以 $d = 1/2$。

label.en: Hamming distance is $1/6$.
label.zh: Hamming 距离是 $1/6$。

feedback.en: Hamming is a count, not a fraction: it is $1$. Dividing by $m$ gives the simple matching distance.
feedback.zh: Hamming 是个计数，不是比例：它是 $1$。除以 $m$ 才是简单匹配距离。

explain.en: Matching: 5 of 6 agree, so $1 - 5/6 = 1/6$. Jaccard: $1 - 1/2$. Same pair, very different distances; the choice should follow what a 0 means.
explain.zh: 匹配：6 个里 5 个一致，$1 - 5/6 = 1/6$。Jaccard：$1 - 1/2$。同一对样本，距离差很多；该怎么选，取决于 0 代表什么。

alt.en: Two points a = (1,5) and b = (5,3). Manhattan distance follows the grid, 4 + 2 = 6. Euclidean distance is the straight line, 4.47.
alt.zh: 两点 a = (1,5) 与 b = (5,3)。曼哈顿距离沿格子走，4 + 2 = 6；欧氏距离是直线，4.47。

items.en: **Manhattan** (L1, city-block): walk along the axes and add up each feature's gap. One huge gap counts only linearly.
items.zh: **曼哈顿**（L1，街区）：沿坐标轴走，把每个特征的差距加起来。一个很大的差距只按线性计入。

items.en: **Euclidean** (L2): the straight line. Squaring makes a large gap in one feature count much more than several small gaps.
items.zh: **欧氏**（L2）：直线距离。平方让某个特征上的大差距比几个小差距重要得多。

text.en: Cosine: the angle, not the length
text.zh: 余弦：看夹角，不看长度

blocks.tex: \cos(a,b) = \frac{a\cdot b}{\lVert a\rVert\,\lVert b\rVert} = \frac{\sum_i a_i b_i}{\sqrt{\sum_i a_i^2}\sqrt{\sum_i b_i^2}} \qquad d(a,b) = 1 - \cos(a,b)

text.en: Divide each vector by its own length, then take the inner product. What is left is only the **direction**. Use it when the length is an accident: a long and a short document about the same topic have different word counts but point the same way; a high- and a low-resolution image of the same scene likewise.
text.zh: 先把每个向量除以自己的长度，再做内积。剩下的只有**方向**。长度只是偶然时就用它：同一主题的长文档和短文档词数不同，但方向一致；同一场景的高分辨率和低分辨率图像也是这样。

prompt.en: Document $b$ is document $a$ with every word count multiplied by 10 (ten times as long). Which distances between $a$ and $b$ are zero?
prompt.zh: 文档 $b$ 是文档 $a$ 的每个词频乘以 10（长了十倍）。$a$ 与 $b$ 之间哪些距离为零？

label.en: Euclidean and Manhattan
label.zh: 欧氏和曼哈顿

feedback.en: They grow with the length: the gap in every coordinate is now 9 times the old count. Only the direction is shared.
feedback.zh: 它们随长度增长：每个坐标上的差现在是原词频的 9 倍。共享的只有方向。

label.en: Cosine only
label.zh: 只有余弦

label.en: All three
label.zh: 三个都是

feedback.en: L1 and L2 see two points far apart on the same ray; only cosine ignores how far along the ray they are.
feedback.zh: L1 和 L2 看到的是同一条射线上相隔很远的两点；只有余弦不管它们在射线上走了多远。

explain.en: $\cos(a, 10a) = 1$, so $d = 0$. The two points are far apart in space yet identical in direction.
explain.zh: $\cos(a, 10a) = 1$，所以 $d = 0$。两点在空间里相隔很远，方向却完全一样。

summary.en: Beyond the deck: all of these are one family
summary.zh: 课件之外：它们是同一族

text.en: Minkowski distance $\left(\sum_i |a_i - b_i|^p\right)^{1/p}$ gives L1 at $p = 1$ and L2 at $p = 2$; as $p \to \infty$ it becomes the largest single gap (Chebyshev). Larger $p$ lets one big gap dominate more.
text.zh: 闵可夫斯基距离 $\left(\sum_i |a_i - b_i|^p\right)^{1/p}$，$p = 1$ 是 L1，$p = 2$ 是 L2；$p \to \infty$ 时就是最大的那一个差（切比雪夫）。$p$ 越大，单个大差距越占主导。

title.en: Deeper: cosine distance, and why it is a Euclidean distance in disguise
title.zh: 深入：余弦距离，以及它为什么是“伪装的欧氏距离”

say.en: Scale each vector to length 1. This throws away the length and keeps the direction.
say.zh: 把每个向量缩放到长度 1。长度被丢掉，方向被留下。

lines.tex: \lVert \hat a - \hat b\rVert^2 = \lVert\hat a\rVert^2 + \lVert\hat b\rVert^2 - 2\,\hat a\cdot\hat b

say.en: Expand the squared Euclidean distance of the two unit vectors: $(u - v)\cdot(u - v)$.
say.zh: 展开两个单位向量的欧氏距离平方：$(u - v)\cdot(u - v)$。

say.en: Both lengths are 1, and $\hat a\cdot\hat b$ is exactly $\cos(a,b)$.
say.zh: 两个长度都是 1，而 $\hat a\cdot\hat b$ 恰好就是 $\cos(a,b)$。

say.en: The bracket is the cosine distance. So on unit-length vectors, cosine distance is half the squared Euclidean distance.
say.zh: 括号里就是余弦距离。所以在单位向量上，余弦距离就是欧氏距离平方的一半。

why.en: Consequence: if you normalise every vector to length 1 first, nearest neighbours under L2 and under cosine are the same. Cosine k-NN is Euclidean k-NN on normalised data.
why.zh: 推论：先把所有向量归一化到长度 1，L2 下的近邻和余弦下的近邻就是同一批。余弦 k-NN 就是归一化数据上的欧氏 k-NN。

say.en: The deck's documents (word counts of three words): doc1 = (200, 300, 200), doc2 = (300, 200, 100). Numerator 140000, lengths $412.3$ and $374.2$.
Small: the two documents mostly use the three words in similar proportions.
say.zh: 很小：两篇文档里三个词的比例大致相近。

say.en: doc3 is much shorter (50, 40, 25) yet points almost exactly the way doc2 does. Under L2 it would be far from doc2; under cosine it is the closest pair.
say.zh: doc3 短得多（50, 40, 25），方向却和 doc2 几乎一样。用 L2 它离 doc2 很远；用余弦它们是最近的一对。

intro.en: Cosine looks different from L1 and L2, but it is nearly one of them. Show how, then do the deck's document example.
intro.zh: 余弦看起来和 L1、L2 不同，其实几乎就是其中一个。先推出这点，再算课件里的文档例子。

text.en: A rating from $-2$ to $2$ has an order but no meaningful gaps: is the step from 0 to 1 the same size as from $-2$ to $-1$? Do not use the raw numbers as if they were measurements. The deck's recipe:
text.zh: 从 $-2$ 到 $2$ 的评分有顺序，但“差多少”没有意义：从 0 到 1 和从 $-2$ 到 $-1$ 一样大吗？不要把原始数字当作测量值来用。课件的做法：

items.en: Sort the possible values and give each a rank $r \in \{0, \dots, m\}$ ($m$ is the largest rank).
items.zh: 把可能的取值排序，给每个取值一个名次 $r \in \{0, \dots, m\}$（$m$ 是最大名次）。

items.en: Map the rank to an evenly spaced value $z = r/m \in [0,1]$.
items.zh: 把名次映射成均匀间隔的数 $z = r/m \in [0,1]$。

items.en: Apply a numeric distance (for example Euclidean) to the $z$ values.
items.zh: 对 $z$ 用数值距离（比如欧氏）。

text.en: Ratings $-2, -1, 0, 1, 2$ have ranks $0, 1, 2, 3, 4$, so $m = 4$. Two cars rated on safety, comfort, convenience: A = $(0, -2, -1)$ and B = $(2, 1, 2)$. Ranks: A = $(2, 0, 1)$, B = $(4, 3, 4)$. Normalised: A = $(0.50, 0.00, 0.25)$, B = $(1.00, 0.75, 1.00)$.
One side effect is useful: every ordinal feature now lives on the same $[0,1]$ scale, which is the next worry (scaling) solved in advance.
text.zh: 顺带有个好处：每个有序特征现在都在同一个 $[0,1]$ 尺度上，后面要讲的缩放问题也就提前解决了。

title.en: When neighbours disagree: three voting rules
title.zh: 近邻意见不一：三种投票规则

text.en: Once the $k$ neighbours are found, each casts a vote for its own class, with a weight $w_j$. The class with the largest **total weight** wins. (For regression, the prediction is the weighted average $\sum_j w_j y_j / \sum_j w_j$.)
text.zh: 找到 $k$ 个近邻后，每个近邻为自己的类别投票，票重为 $w_j$。**总票重**最大的类别获胜。（回归则取加权平均 $\sum_j w_j y_j / \sum_j w_j$。）

head.zh: 第 j 个近邻的票重

rows.en: nearest gets 1, farthest of the k gets 0
rows.zh: 最近的得 1，k 个里最远的得 0

items.en: $\epsilon$ is a tiny constant (the deck uses $10^{-10}$ or $10^{-5}$) that keeps $1/d$ finite when a neighbour sits exactly on the query ($d = 0$).
items.zh: $\epsilon$ 是个很小的常数（课件用 $10^{-10}$ 或 $10^{-5}$），当某个近邻恰好落在查询点上（$d = 0$）时防止 $1/d$ 变成无穷。

items.en: In inverse linear distance, $d_1$ is the smallest and $d_k$ the largest distance among the $k$ neighbours. The weights are a straight line from 1 down to 0, so the farthest neighbour never counts and the rule needs $d_k \neq d_1$.
items.zh: 反线性距离里，$d_1$ 是 $k$ 个近邻中最小的距离，$d_k$ 是最大的。权重是从 1 线性降到 0 的一条直线，所以最远的那个近邻不起作用，并且要求 $d_k \neq d_1$。

items.en: Inverse distance is a very strong rule: a neighbour at distance $\approx 0$ gets weight $10^5$ and outvotes everyone. Inverse linear is gentler.
items.zh: 反距离是很强的规则：距离 $\approx 0$ 的近邻拿到 $10^5$ 的权重，一个人就压过所有人。反线性要温和得多。

text.en: The deck's example has $K = 4$ neighbours: one red at distance 0 and three blue at distances 1, 1.5, 1.5. Three rules, three recipes, and not the same answer. Next page: the arithmetic.
text.zh: 课件里的例子有 $K = 4$ 个近邻：一个红色在距离 0，三个蓝色分别在距离 1、1.5、1.5。三种规则，三种算法，答案并不一样。下一页算一遍。

title.en: The deck's voting example, line by line
title.zh: 课件的投票例子，一行一行算

say.en: Majority vote: all weights 1, count heads. $W_R$ and $W_B$ are the total weights of red and blue. Blue has three neighbours, red one, so blue wins.
say.zh: 权重全是 1，数人头。$W_R$、$W_B$ 是红、蓝的总票重。蓝色三个近邻，红色一个，蓝色获胜。

say.en: Inverse distance, $\epsilon = 10^{-5}$. The red neighbour sits at distance 0, so its weight is huge.
say.zh: 反距离，$\epsilon = 10^{-5}$。红色近邻在距离 0，权重极大。

say.en: The three blue weights, one for each neighbour.
say.zh: 三个蓝色近邻各自的权重。

say.en: Add up the blue votes (the deck prints 2.34 after rounding each term up). Red $\approx 100000$ beats blue $\approx 2.3$: **red wins**.
say.zh: 把蓝色的票相加（课件把每项进位后写成 2.34）。红 $\approx 100000$ 压倒蓝 $\approx 2.3$：**红色获胜**。

say.en: Inverse linear distance: here $d_1 = 0$ (red) and $d_k = 1.5$ (the farthest), so each weight is $(1.5 - d_j)/1.5$.
say.zh: 反线性距离：这里 $d_1 = 0$（红色），$d_k = 1.5$（最远的），所以每个权重是 $(1.5 - d_j)/1.5$。

say.en: The nearest neighbour always gets exactly 1.
say.zh: 最近的近邻永远恰好得 1。

say.en: The two blue neighbours at the maximum distance get weight 0. Only the one at distance 1 counts. (The deck rounds this to 0.3.)
say.zh: 处在最大距离的两个蓝色近邻得权重 0，只有距离 1 的那个起作用。（课件把它舍入成 0.3。）

say.en: Compare totals: red 1, blue 0.33, so red wins. Two of the three rules pick red, and majority picks blue. The same neighbours can give different predictions depending on the rule.
say.zh: 比较总票重：红 1，蓝 0.33，红色获胜。三种规则里两种选红，多数票选蓝。同样的近邻，规则不同，预测可以不同。

intro.en: Neighbours (class, distance): (red, 0), (blue, 1), (blue, 1.5), (blue, 1.5). Compute the winner under each rule.
intro.zh: 近邻（类别，距离）：(red, 0)、(blue, 1)、(blue, 1.5)、(blue, 1.5)。求每种规则下的赢家。

prompt.en: Blue's total weight under inverse linear distance: the weights are $(1.5 - d_j)/1.5$ for $d_j = 1, 1.5, 1.5$.

title.en: Ties: tied distances and tied votes
title.zh: 平局：距离相同与票数相同

text.en: The deck shows two kinds of tie on a plot of points. Both are real, and an answer must say how you resolve them; the slides give no single rule, so these are the standard options.
text.zh: 课件在散点图上给出两种平局。两种都真实存在，答题时要说明怎么处理；课件没有给唯一的规则，下面是通行的做法。

rows.en: 1-NN, but two points are exactly as close
take both (the neighbourhood grows beyond k); or pick at random; or keep the one stored first
rows.zh: 两个都取（近邻数超过 k）；或随机选；或取先存的那个

rows.en: use an odd k (two classes); or drop to k−1 / grow to k+1 until broken; or use distance weights; or pick the class more common in training (the prior); or random
rows.zh: 用奇数 k（两类时）；或降到 k−1 / 升到 k+1 直到打破；或用距离加权；或取训练集里更常见的类（先验）；或随机

text.en: Distance-weighted voting breaks most vote ties for free, because two neighbours are almost never at exactly the same distance. That is one practical reason to prefer it.
text.zh: 按距离加权的投票几乎白送地打破了票数相同的平局，因为两个近邻几乎不会恰好一样远。这是选用它的一个实际理由。

prompt.en: A 3-class problem with $k = 3$ and neighbours of classes A, B, C (one each). Choosing an odd $k$ avoided the tie. Why not?
prompt.zh: 3 类问题，$k = 3$，近邻的类别是 A、B、C 各一个。选了奇数 $k$ 却没避免平局。为什么？

label.en: $k$ must be a multiple of the number of classes.
label.zh: $k$ 必须是类别数的倍数。

feedback.en: Not so: a multiple of 3 still allows 2-2-2 splits. No $k$ rules out ties for 3+ classes.
feedback.zh: 不对：3 的倍数仍可能 2-2-2 平分。类别数 ≥ 3 时没有哪个 $k$ 能排除平局。

label.en: Odd $k$ never helps.
label.zh: 奇数 $k$ 从不起作用。

feedback.en: It does help for two classes: $k$ neighbours split $a + b = k$, and with $k$ odd, $a \neq b$.
feedback.zh: 两类时有用：$k$ 个近邻分成 $a + b = k$，$k$ 为奇数则 $a \neq b$。

label.en: An odd $k$ only prevents ties when there are two classes.
label.zh: 奇数 $k$ 只在两类时才能避免平局。

explain.en: With two classes an odd $k$ guarantees a winner; with three or more you still need a tie rule (weights, prior, random).
explain.zh: 两类时奇数 $k$ 保证有赢家；三类或更多仍需要平局规则（加权、先验、随机）。

text.en: $k$ decides how local the answer is. $k = 1$: the single nearest point. $k = N$: every training point, whatever the query. The figure runs both extremes and a middle value on the same data.
text.zh: $k$ 决定答案有多“局部”。$k = 1$：只看最近的一个点。$k = N$：不管查询点在哪，都看全部训练点。下图在同一份数据上跑这两个极端和一个中间值。

alt.en: Decision regions of k-NN on 31 points of two classes, for k = 1, k = 7, k = N. k = 1 is jagged with islands around single points; k = 7 is smooth; k = N colours the whole plane with the majority class.
alt.zh: 两类共 31 个点上 k 近邻的决策区域，k = 1、k = 7、k = N。k = 1 锯齿状，围着单个点形成孤岛；k = 7 平滑；k = N 整个平面都是多数类的颜色。

items.en: **Small $k$**: a jagged boundary that follows every point, including the noisy and mislabelled ones. We capture noise, so test performance drops.
items.zh: **小 $k$**：边界锯齿状，紧跟每一个点，包括噪声点和标错的点。我们把噪声也学进去了，测试表现下降。

items.en: **Large $k$**: a smooth boundary, but it risks grouping together unrelated classes; test performance drops again.
items.zh: **大 $k$**：边界平滑，但可能把无关的类别混在一起；测试表现又会下降。

items.en: **$k = N$**: every query gets the same answer, the most common class in the training set. That is the **Zero-R** baseline of the trees lesson, ignoring all features.
items.zh: **$k = N$**：每个查询得到同一个答案，即训练集中最常见的类别。这就是决策树那一课的 **Zero-R** 基线，完全不看特征。

text.en: So test error against $k$ is U-shaped. **Choose $k$ on held-out data** (a validation set or cross-validation), never on the training set: with $k = 1$ every training point is its own nearest neighbour, so training error is $0$ and $k = 1$ always “wins” there. Try odd values for two classes, and keep $k$ well below $N$.
text.zh: 所以测试误差随 $k$ 变化呈 U 形。**用留出数据选 $k$**（验证集或交叉验证），不要用训练集：$k = 1$ 时每个训练点的最近邻就是它自己，训练误差为 $0$，$k = 1$ 在训练集上永远“最好”。两类时试奇数值，并让 $k$ 远小于 $N$。

prompt.en: You pick $k$ by lowest training error. Which $k$ do you get, and why is that a mistake?
prompt.zh: 你按训练误差最低来选 $k$。会选到哪个 $k$，为什么是错的？

label.en: $k = N$: it uses all the data.
label.zh: $k = N$：它用了全部数据。

feedback.en: $k = N$ ignores the query completely, so it does worst on training data, not best.
feedback.zh: $k = N$ 完全不看查询点，训练数据上反而最差。

label.en: A middle $k$ near $\sqrt{N}$, which is always optimal.
label.zh: $\sqrt{N}$ 附近的中间值，它总是最优。

feedback.en: There is no universally optimal $k$; it depends on the data and has to be validated.
feedback.zh: 并不存在放之四海皆准的最优 $k$；它取决于数据，必须用验证来定。

label.en: $k = 1$: each training point finds itself, so training error is 0. It says nothing about new data.
label.zh: $k = 1$：每个训练点找到的就是自己，训练误差为 0。这对新数据什么也没说明。

explain.en: Training error only tells you how well the data was memorised. Use a validation set to choose $k$.
explain.zh: 训练误差只说明数据被记住了多少。要用验证集来选 $k$。

title.en: Deeper: why k is a bias-variance knob
title.zh: 深入：为什么 k 是偏差-方差旋钮

say.en: The model of the data: the truth $f$ plus independent noise of variance $\sigma^2$. We predict at a fixed query $x_0$.
say.zh: 数据的模型：真实函数 $f$ 加上方差为 $\sigma^2$ 的独立噪声。我们在固定的查询点 $x_0$ 上预测。

say.en: k-NN regression averages the $k$ neighbours' labels. Each label carries its own noise $\varepsilon_i$.
say.zh: k-NN 回归对 $k$ 个近邻的标签取平均。每个标签带着自己的噪声 $\varepsilon_i$。

say.en: The bias $b$: the noise averages to zero, so the prediction is off on average only because the neighbours' true values differ from $f(x_0)$. For $k=1$ this gap is small (the neighbour is very close); as $k$ grows the neighbours lie farther out and the gap grows. For $k = N$ it is $\bar f - f(x_0)$.
say.zh: 偏差 $b$：噪声平均为零，所以预测平均而言出偏差，只是因为近邻的真值与 $f(x_0)$ 不同。$k = 1$ 时这个差很小（近邻很近）；$k$ 增大，近邻越来越远，差变大。$k = N$ 时是 $\bar f - f(x_0)$。

say.en: Independent noises: the variance of a sum is the sum of variances, and the factor $1/k$ is squared. Averaging $k$ noisy numbers divides the variance by $k$.
say.zh: 噪声相互独立：和的方差是方差的和，系数 $1/k$ 要平方。把 $k$ 个带噪的数取平均，方差就除以 $k$。

say.en: The expected squared error at $x_0$ splits into noise we can never remove, squared bias, and variance.
say.zh: 在 $x_0$ 处的期望平方误差分成三块：永远去不掉的噪声、偏差的平方、方差。

say.en: At $k = 1$ the variance is the largest ($\sigma^2$), at $k = N$ the smallest but with the largest bias. The knob: raising $k$ cuts the variance like $1/k$ and raises the bias. The best $k$ balances the two. This is the same picture as the figure: $k=1$ is jagged because it has high variance; $k=N$ is flat because it has high bias.
say.zh: $k = 1$ 方差最大（$\sigma^2$），$k = N$ 方差最小但偏差最大。旋钮：升高 $k$，方差按 $1/k$ 下降，偏差上升。最优的 $k$ 在二者之间取平衡。这就是上图的另一种说法：$k=1$ 锯齿是因为方差大；$k=N$ 一片平是因为偏差大。

intro.en: The U-shaped test error is not a coincidence. Show it for k-NN regression with a few lines, assuming the training inputs are fixed.
intro.zh: U 形的测试误差并非巧合。用几行推导在 k-NN 回归上把它写出来，假设训练输入固定。

title.zh: 缩放：数值最大的特征说了算

text.en: Distance adds the features' gaps up, so a feature measured in big numbers shouts over one measured in small numbers, whatever each is worth. The units are arbitrary (income in dollars or in thousands of dollars?), so the answer must not depend on them.
text.zh: 距离把各特征的差距加起来，所以用大数字量的特征会盖过用小数字量的特征，不管它们各自有多重要。单位是任意的（收入用美元还是千美元？），答案不该依赖单位。

text.en: A numeric example. The query is a customer aged 30 with income \$50,000. Customer A is aged 31 with income \$58,000; customer B is aged 60 with income \$50,500.
text.zh: 一个数值例子。查询客户 30 岁，收入 50,000 美元。客户 A 31 岁，收入 58,000 美元；客户 B 60 岁，收入 50,500 美元。

text.en: Raw: income gaps are in the thousands, age gaps in the tens, so age is invisible and the 30-year-older B is “closest”. Min-max scaling with ranges age $[18, 70]$, income $[20,000, 120,000]$ maps both to $[0,1]$, and now A, nearly the same age, is nearest. The flip changes the prediction.
text.zh: 原始数据里，收入差是几千，年龄差是几十，年龄几乎看不见，于是大了 30 岁的 B 成了“最近”。用年龄范围 $[18, 70]$、收入范围 $[20,000, 120,000]$ 做最小-最大缩放，两者都落在 $[0,1]$，年龄几乎相同的 A 才是最近的。这一翻转改变了预测。

items.en: **Min-max** (the first formula) puts every feature in $[0,1]$ but one outlier squeezes all the others together.
items.zh: **最小-最大**（第一个公式）把每个特征放进 $[0,1]$，但一个离群点会把其余的点全挤在一起。

items.en: **z-score** (the second; mean 0, standard deviation 1) is steadier under outliers.
items.zh: **z 分数**（第二个；均值 0、标准差 1）对离群点更稳。

items.en: Compute $x_{\min}, x_{\max}$ (or $\mu, s$) **on the training data only** and apply the same numbers to the test instance; otherwise information leaks from the test set.
items.zh: $x_{\min}, x_{\max}$（或 $\mu, s$）**只用训练数据**来算，再把同样的数用到测试样本上；否则测试集的信息会泄漏。

items.en: Scaling is also a way to say what matters: multiplying a feature by 2 after scaling doubles its say in the distance.
items.zh: 缩放也是表达“什么重要”的方式：缩放后把某个特征乘以 2，它在距离里的话语权就翻倍。

prompt.en: Features: height in metres (1.5-2.0) and weight in grams (50,000-100,000). With raw Euclidean distance, which feature decides the neighbours?
prompt.zh: 特征：身高（米，1.5-2.0）和体重（克，50,000-100,000）。用原始欧氏距离，哪个特征决定近邻？

label.en: Height: it is the more informative one.
label.zh: 身高：它信息量更大。

feedback.en: Distance does not know which feature is informative; it only sees the size of the numbers.
feedback.zh: 距离并不知道哪个特征有信息，它只看数字的大小。

label.en: Weight: its gaps are about $10^4$ times bigger.
label.zh: 体重：它的差距大约是 $10^4$ 倍。

label.en: Neither: Euclidean distance is scale-invariant.
label.zh: 都不是：欧氏距离与尺度无关。

feedback.en: It is the opposite: rescaling a feature changes the distances, so changes the neighbours.
feedback.zh: 恰恰相反：改变特征的尺度会改变距离，从而改变近邻。

explain.en: Scale first. Then both features contribute comparably.
explain.zh: 先缩放。之后两个特征的贡献才相当。

text.en: k-NN trusts that near points are alike. In many dimensions, *nothing is near*. Two things happen at once:
text.zh: k-NN 相信“靠得近的点相似”。维度很多时，*没有什么是近的*。同时发生两件事：

text.en: 1. You need to reach far to catch a few points
text.zh: 1. 要伸得很远才能抓到几个点

text.en: Points uniform in the unit cube $[0,1]^d$. A small cube that catches 10% of the data has edge length $0.1^{1/d}$:
text.zh: 点在单位立方体 $[0,1]^d$ 中均匀分布。能装下 10% 数据的小立方体，边长是 $0.1^{1/d}$：

text.en: At $d = 100$ the “neighbourhood” spans 98% of the range of every coordinate: it is not a neighbourhood any more.
text.zh: $d = 100$ 时，这个“邻域”在每个坐标上都占去 98% 的范围：它已经不是邻域了。

text.en: 2. All distances become the same
text.zh: 2. 所有距离都变得一样

text.en: Draw 100 uniform points and a query. The table is the average of (nearest distance) / (farthest distance) over 200 trials (seeded simulation). If it is near 0, “nearest” means something. If near 1, it does not.
text.zh: 取 100 个均匀分布的点和一个查询点。表中是 200 次试验里（最近距离）/（最远距离）的平均（固定随机种子的模拟）。接近 0，“最近”才有意义；接近 1，就没有了。

alt.en: The average ratio of nearest to farthest distance among 100 random points rises towards 1 as the dimension d grows from 1 to 1000.
alt.zh: 100 个随机点中，最近距离与最远距离之比的平均值，随维度 d 从 1 增到 1000 而趋近于 1。

text.en: The next page proves why the ratio tends to 1. Practical consequences:
text.zh: 下一页证明为什么这个比值趋于 1。实际的后果：

items.en: Irrelevant features are poison: each adds noise to the distance and pushes everything toward the same value.
items.zh: 无关特征是毒药：每多一个，距离里就多一份噪声，把一切推向同一个值。

items.en: Fixes: select or reduce features (feature selection, PCA), use more data (the amount needed grows exponentially with $d$), or use a measure suited to sparse data (cosine).
items.zh: 对策：特征选择或降维（PCA）、增加数据（所需数据量随 $d$ 指数增长），或用适合稀疏数据的度量（余弦）。

items.en: Real data often lies near a low-dimensional surface, which is why k-NN still works on images with thousands of pixels.
items.zh: 真实数据往往靠近一个低维曲面，这就是 k-NN 在有上千像素的图像上仍然有效的原因。

title.zh: 深入：距离为什么会集中

say.en: Two independent uniform points $x, y \in [0,1]^d$. The squared distance is a sum of $d$ terms, one per coordinate. The terms are independent and identically distributed.
say.zh: 两个独立的均匀点 $x, y \in [0,1]^d$。距离平方是 $d$ 项之和，每个坐标一项。这些项独立同分布。

say.en: For independent $x, y$ with the same mean, $\mathbb{E}[(x-y)^2] = \mathrm{Var}(x) + \mathrm{Var}(y)$. A uniform variable on $[0,1]$ has variance $1/12$.
say.zh: 独立且均值相同的 $x, y$，$\mathbb{E}[(x-y)^2] = \mathrm{Var}(x) + \mathrm{Var}(y)$。$[0,1]$ 上的均匀变量方差是 $1/12$。

say.en: The fourth moment of $x - y$ (a triangular density on $[-1,1]$) is $1/15$. Subtract the square of the mean.
say.zh: $x - y$（$[-1,1]$ 上的三角形密度）的四阶矩是 $1/15$。减去均值的平方。

say.en: A sum of $d$ independent terms: means add, variances add.
say.zh: $d$ 个独立项之和：均值相加，方差相加。

say.en: The relative spread. The mean grows like $d$ but the standard deviation only like $\sqrt d$, so the spread shrinks like $1/\sqrt d$. At $d = 100$: 12%; at $d = 1000$: 3.7%.
say.zh: 相对离散程度。均值按 $d$ 增长，标准差只按 $\sqrt d$ 增长，所以离散程度按 $1/\sqrt d$ 缩小。$d = 100$：12%；$d = 1000$：3.7%。

say.en: Every distance is almost the same, so the nearest point is hardly nearer than the farthest. “Nearest” carries almost no information, and the vote of the $k$ nearest is close to a vote of random points.
say.zh: 每一对点的距离几乎一样，最近的点并不比最远的近多少。“最近”几乎没有信息，$k$ 个最近邻的投票和随机点的投票差不多。

intro.en: Why does the nearest / farthest ratio in the table tend to 1? It is the law of large numbers applied to a sum over coordinates.
intro.zh: 表里的“最近 / 最远”为什么趋于 1？这是大数定律用在各坐标的和上。

title.en: Lazy against eager, and the verdict
title.zh: 惰性与积极，以及最后的评价

rows.en: fit a model to the labelled data
rows.zh: 用带标签的数据拟合模型

rows.en: a distance function and a prediction rule
compare the test instance with every stored instance
rows.zh: 把测试样本与每个存下的样本比较

rows.en: decision trees, naive Bayes, regression, SVM, neural nets
rows.zh: 决策树、朴素贝叶斯、回归、SVM、神经网络

items.en: **No assumptions**: k-NN does not assume a shape for the boundary. It is *non-parametric*: its complexity grows with the data, not fixed in advance.
items.zh: **没有假设**：k-NN 不预设边界的形状。它是*非参数*的：复杂度随数据增长，而不是事先固定。

items.en: **No training**: new data evolves the model immediately; you just add a row.
items.zh: **不用训练**：新数据立刻改变模型，加一行就行。

items.en: **Cost**: each prediction scans all $N$ instances ($O(NF)$ time) and the whole data set must be kept in memory. Expensive for large or growing data (indexes such as k-d trees help in low dimensions; they fail in the high dimensions above).
items.zh: **代价**：每次预测要扫描全部 $N$ 个样本（$O(NF)$ 时间），整份数据都得放在内存里。数据大或不断增长时很贵（k-d 树这类索引在低维时有用，在上面说的高维里失效）。

rows.en: No training: adapts at once to new data
rows.zh: 没有训练：立刻适应新数据

rows.en: Expensive for large or growing data sets
rows.zh: 数据大或持续增长时代价高

text.en: Add to the deck's cons the two we proved: it needs scaled features and it degrades in high dimensions.
text.zh: 在课件列出的缺点之外，再加上我们证明过的两条：需要缩放特征，并且在高维下性能下降。

prompt.en: $a = (3, 1, 4)$ and $b = (1, 5, 2)$. What is their Euclidean distance? Round to 2 decimals.
prompt.zh: $a = (3, 1, 4)$，$b = (1, 5, 2)$。它们的欧氏距离是多少？保留 2 位小数。

explain.en: Gaps $2, -4, 2$; squares $4 + 16 + 4 = 24$; $\sqrt{24} = 4.899$. The Manhattan distance is $2 + 4 + 2 = 8$.

prompt.en: $k = 4$ neighbours (class, distance): (A, 1), (B, 2), (B, 3), (A, 5). Using inverse linear distance weights, what is the total weight of class B?
prompt.zh: $k = 4$ 个近邻（类别，距离）：(A, 1)、(B, 2)、(B, 3)、(A, 5)。用反线性距离权重，B 类的总票重是多少？

explain.en: $d_1 = 1$, $d_k = 5$, so $w = (5 - d)/4$: A gets $1$ and $0$ (total 1.00), B gets $0.75$ and $0.5$ (total 1.25). **B wins** though both classes have two neighbours. Majority voting would tie; inverse distance would pick A (1.20 against 0.83).

prompt.en: A k-NN classifier is run with $k = N$ (the number of training instances), majority vote. What does it predict for a new instance?
prompt.zh: 用 $k = N$（训练样本总数）、多数票运行 k-NN 分类器。它对新样本预测什么？

label.en: The class of the nearest training instance.
label.zh: 最近训练样本的类别。

feedback.en: That is $k = 1$. With $k = N$ the neighbours are everyone.
feedback.zh: 那是 $k = 1$。$k = N$ 时近邻是所有人。

label.en: The majority class of the whole training set, for every query.
label.zh: 整个训练集的多数类，对每个查询都一样。

label.en: A smooth boundary that separates the classes best.
label.zh: 一条把各类分得最好的平滑边界。

feedback.en: There is no boundary: the answer never changes with the query. It is maximal bias, and the Zero-R baseline.
feedback.zh: 根本没有边界：答案不随查询点变化。这是偏差最大，也就是 Zero-R 基线。

label.en: It overfits the most.
label.zh: 它过拟合得最厉害。

feedback.en: The opposite: it underfits the most (high bias, zero adaptivity). $k = 1$ overfits the most.
feedback.zh: 相反：它欠拟合得最厉害（高偏差，毫无适应性）。过拟合最厉害的是 $k = 1$。

explain.en: With $k = N$ every training instance votes, whatever the query: the prediction is the training majority class.
explain.zh: $k = N$ 时每个训练样本都投票，与查询点无关：预测就是训练集的多数类。

prompt.en: You add 900 irrelevant random features to a k-NN problem with 10 informative ones, and the data set size stays the same. What happens, and why?
prompt.zh: 在一个有 10 个有用特征的 k-NN 问题上再加 900 个无关的随机特征，数据量不变。会发生什么，为什么？

label.en: Accuracy improves: more features give more information.
label.zh: 准确率提高：更多特征带来更多信息。

feedback.en: Irrelevant features carry no information, only noise that enters every distance.
feedback.zh: 无关特征没有信息，只给每个距离加噪声。

label.en: Nothing changes: distance ignores features that do not matter.
label.zh: 没有变化：距离会忽略不重要的特征。

feedback.en: Distance cannot tell which features matter; each of the 900 adds its share to the sum.
feedback.zh: 距离分不出哪些特征重要；900 个特征每个都往和里加一份。

label.en: Accuracy drops: the 900 noise coordinates dominate the distances, which concentrate, so the neighbours stop being the truly similar points.
label.zh: 准确率下降：900 个噪声坐标主导了距离，而距离会集中，近邻不再是真正相似的点。

label.en: Only training time increases, the predictions stay the same.
label.zh: 只是训练时间变长，预测不变。

feedback.en: k-NN has no training time, and the neighbours themselves change.
feedback.zh: k-NN 没有训练时间，而且近邻本身变了。

explain.en: This is the curse of dimensionality seen as feature noise. Feature selection or scaling down the irrelevant features is the cure.
explain.zh: 这就是特征噪声形态的维度灾难。对策是特征选择，或把无关特征的尺度压下去。

prompt.en: Explain how the choice of $k$ affects a k-NN classifier, and how you would choose it.
prompt.zh: 解释 $k$ 的选择如何影响 k-NN 分类器，以及你怎么选 $k$。

key_points.en: small k: jagged boundary, fits noise, high variance (overfits)
key_points.zh: 小 k：边界锯齿，拟合噪声，高方差（过拟合）

key_points.en: large k: smooth boundary, may merge classes, high bias (underfits); k = N is the majority class
key_points.zh: 大 k：边界平滑，可能混淆类别，高偏差（欠拟合）；k = N 就是多数类

key_points.en: choose k on validation data / cross-validation, not training error
key_points.zh: 用验证数据或交叉验证选 k，不要用训练误差

model_answer.en: A small k gives a jagged decision boundary that follows noise: low bias but high variance, so it overfits. A large k gives a smooth boundary that may group unrelated classes: high bias, low variance; with k = N every query gets the majority class. I would choose k by validation or cross-validation (never by training error, where k = 1 is always perfect), trying odd values for two classes.
model_answer.zh: k 小，决策边界锯齿状、跟着噪声走：偏差低、方差高，所以过拟合。k 大，边界平滑，可能把不相关的类别混在一起：偏差高、方差低；k = N 时每个查询都得到多数类。我会用验证集或交叉验证选 k（不能用训练误差，因为那样 k = 1 永远完美），两类时试奇数值。

explain.en: Name both failure modes, say which is bias and which is variance, and say that k is chosen on held-out data.
explain.zh: 两种失败方式都要写，说清哪个是偏差哪个是方差，并说明 k 是在留出数据上选的。

prompt.en: You must classify short customer reviews as positive or negative with k-NN. Describe how you would represent the reviews, which distance you would use and why, how you would vote, and one weakness you expect.
prompt.zh: 你要用 k-NN 把简短的顾客评论分成正面或负面。说明：怎么表示评论，用什么距离、为什么，怎么投票，以及你预计的一个弱点。

key_points.en: represent: word-count (or presence) vector over a vocabulary
key_points.zh: 表示：基于词表的词频（或有无）向量

key_points.en: cosine distance: removes the effect of review length (or Jaccard for presence)
key_points.zh: 余弦距离：去掉评论长短的影响（有无向量可用 Jaccard）

key_points.en: vote: odd k chosen by cross-validation, possibly distance-weighted
key_points.zh: 投票：用交叉验证选奇数 k，可按距离加权

key_points.en: weakness: high-dimensional sparse vectors (distances concentrate), slow prediction on large data
key_points.zh: 弱点：高维稀疏向量（距离集中），数据大时预测慢

model_answer.en: I would represent each review as a bag-of-words vector of word counts over a vocabulary (optionally with stop words removed). Reviews differ greatly in length, so I would use cosine distance, which compares the direction of the vectors, not their magnitude. I would use k nearest neighbours with odd k chosen by cross-validation, and weight votes by inverse linear distance to break ties. Weaknesses: the vectors are high-dimensional and sparse, so distances concentrate and many words are irrelevant (feature selection would help), and every prediction scans the whole training set.
model_answer.zh: 我把每条评论表示为基于词表的词袋词频向量（可去掉停用词）。评论长短差别很大，所以用余弦距离，它比较向量的方向而不是大小。用 k 近邻，k 取奇数并用交叉验证选定，投票按反线性距离加权以打破平局。弱点：向量维度高且稀疏，距离会集中，许多词也无关（特征选择会有帮助），而且每次预测都要扫描整个训练集。

explain.en: Four things marked: representation, distance with its reason, voting and k, a weakness. Nothing about the model that is not asked.
explain.zh: 四项给分：表示、距离及理由、投票与 k、一个弱点。不要写没问的内容。

items.en: Voting: majority $w=1$; inverse distance $1/(d+\epsilon)$; inverse linear $(d_k - d_j)/(d_k - d_1)$. Regression: average of the neighbours. Break ties with odd $k$, weights, prior, or randomly.
items.zh: 投票：多数票 $w=1$；反距离 $1/(d+\epsilon)$；反线性 $(d_k - d_j)/(d_k - d_1)$。回归：近邻取平均。平局用奇数 $k$、加权、先验或随机来破。

items.en: $k$: small = jagged, high variance; large = smooth, high bias; $k = N$ = majority class. Choose it on validation data. Variance of the average is $\sigma^2/k$.
items.zh: $k$：小 = 锯齿、高方差；大 = 平滑、高偏差；$k = N$ = 多数类。用验证数据选。平均的方差是 $\sigma^2/k$。

items.en: Scale features (fit the scaler on training data only). In high dimensions distances concentrate: nearest $\approx$ farthest.
items.zh: 要缩放特征（缩放参数只用训练数据拟合）。高维时距离集中：最近 $\approx$ 最远。

items.en: Lazy: store everything, no training, no assumptions, expensive prediction. Ordinal features: normalised rank $r/m$.
items.zh: 惰性：存下一切、不训练、无假设、预测代价高。有序特征：归一化名次 $r/m$。
